title: Cello Concerto No. 1 in A minor
hook: A whole concerto in under twenty minutes, without a pause, starting with a single chord.

painting.title: Impression, Sunrise
painting.pairingNote: Painted at Le Havre around November 1872, the month Saint-Saëns finished his concerto; a morning sun breaking through the mist, set down quickly and in one sweep.

facts: Saint-Saëns finished the concerto in November 1872, when he was 37. He wrote it for the French cellist Auguste Tolbecque, who was also a viola da gamba player and an instrument maker.

Tolbecque played the premiere on 19 January 1873 at a concert of the Paris Conservatoire’s orchestra, the Société des Concerts. Being performed there was a sign that the French musical establishment had accepted Saint-Saëns.
The concerto is one continuous movement in three sections: fast, then a gentle dance, then fast again. Its themes return and are linked across the sections, so the whole work feels like one sweep.

It lasts less than twenty minutes, and it has no orchestral introduction: after one chord the cello plunges straight in. The orchestra is kept light, so the cello is heard clearly in every register, and it has remained a favourite of cellists ever since.
bigPicture.inOneLine: an agitated, rushing opening (I), a delicate old-fashioned minuet with a singing cello above it (II), the rush returns and turns to light at the end (III).

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo – Allegretto con moto – Tempo primo
movements.tempo: Allegro non troppo – Allegretto con moto – Tempo primo
movements.summary: The whole concerto plays as one track and one movement, in three linked sections. A fast, agitated first section introduces a rushing cello theme; a delicate minuet for [[muted|muted]] strings follows; then the rushing theme returns, new melodies join it, and the concerto ends brightly in A major.

mainIdeas.name: The rushing theme
mainIdeas.description: falling groups of three quick notes in the cello, agitated and urgent.

mainIdeas.name: The minuet
mainIdeas.description: a delicate, old-fashioned dance for muted strings, with a long, singing cello line above it.

mainIdeas.name: The calm melody
mainIdeas.description: a slow, rising line in the cello that ends high and glassy.

stops.hear: One short chord from the orchestra; at once the cello rushes in with falling groups of three quick notes
stops.happening: No introduction: the main theme straight away

stops.hear: The cello climbs in quick, pulsing triplets, a little more hopeful
Calmer: the cello plays a slow, rising line that ends on a high, glassy note
The orchestra takes over with a bold, faster theme
stops.happening: A new theme in F major

stops.hear: The rushing theme is passed between cello and orchestra, building in force
The music winds down and slows
stops.happening: The way into the middle section

stops.hear: Muted strings play a delicate, old-fashioned dance, quiet and light
stops.happening: *Allegretto con moto*: a [[minuet|minuet]], in B-flat major

stops.hear: The cello enters with a long, singing line that floats above the dance
stops.happening: The cello’s melody over the minuet

stops.hear: The dance fades, and the cello lingers alone
stops.happening: The end of the middle section

stops.hear: The rushing theme returns in the orchestra, and the cello takes it up
The cello plays a new, broad melody, slower and darker
stops.happening: A new theme in the last section

stops.hear: Fast, brilliant passages for the cello, from its highest notes to its lowest
stops.happening: The most demanding part of the concerto

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The music turns to A major; quick, bright figures and firm closing chords
stops.happening: The ending, minor turned to major

notice: Listen to the very first second. A single chord, and the cello is already playing. There is no orchestral introduction to wait for.
In the minuet, notice how far apart the two layers are: the strings dance lightly and quietly, while the cello sings long notes above them.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Yo-Yo Ma recorded the concerto in Paris in 1980, with Lorin Maazel and the Orchestre National de France. On the Spotify album the concerto is a single track, followed by Lalo’s Cello Concerto.

threads.title: One movement, three sections
threads.body: Saint-Saëns joins fast, slow dance and fast into one continuous piece, a plan that recalls the one-movement works of his friend Liszt.

threads.title: Themes that return
threads.body: The rushing opening comes back at the start of the third section, and the end turns the concerto’s minor key to major.

threads.title: A light orchestra
threads.body: The orchestra is small and the textures are clear, so the cello never has to fight to be heard.
